findings.title: Fire-and-forget goroutine with derived context, no error propagation or sync in tests/production
findings.body: Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection spawn goroutines using context.WithTimeoutCause derived from the request ctx. If the parent ctx (request context) is cancelled when the HTTP response is sent, the derived context will also be cancelled before the legacy write completes, causing the asynchronous legacy write to be silently aborted (not after 10s, but immediately on request completion). This defeats the stated goal of 'write to legacy asynchronously as a safe measure' since most of the time the write will be cancelled right after the response is returned.

findings.title: Legacy write errors are silently swallowed
findings.body: In Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection, errors from the asynchronous legacy write are only recorded in a duration metric (recordLegacyDuration) but never logged or surfaced anywhere else. If legacy writes to the fallback store start failing consistently, there is no log signal to catch it, undermining the 'safe measure' purpose of still writing to legacy.

findings.title: Delete ignores constructed log context
findings.body: In Delete, a logger with method/kind/name values is built into `log`, but `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` uses `d.Log` instead of the local `log` variable, so the extra context fields (name, kind, method) are not propagated into the context used by subsequent calls.

findings.title: Incorrect metric call on storage update failure
findings.body: In Update, when d.Storage.Update fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) instead of d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...). This mislabels a storage failure as a legacy failure in metrics, making mode3 dashboards/alerts inaccurate.

findings.title: Incorrect metric call on storage create failure
findings.body: In Create, when d.Storage.Create fails, the code calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...) rather than d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...), mislabeling the failure source in telemetry.

findings.title: Shadowed metrics registry causes duplicate registration risk
findings.body: In TestMode3_Get a new prometheus.NewRegistry() `p` is created locally shadowing the package-level `p`, inconsistent with other subtests in the same file that reuse the shared `p`. This is unnecessary and can mask registration-collision bugs that would otherwise be caught by reusing a single registry across test cases within the same process.

findings.title: No tests verify asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: The new DualWriterMode3 implementation performs legacy writes in background goroutines for Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection, but none of the tests assert that the legacy mock's Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection methods are actually invoked (e.g., via m.AssertExpectations or similar with a wait). Since these calls happen asynchronously, the tests may pass even if the goroutine logic is broken, is never triggered, or has a race condition — leaving the core new behavior of mode 3 untested.
